channel.title: Zoes blog
channel.description: Guides and fair comparisons for running Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents in parallel, from the people who build Zoes.

item.title: How to move a Claude Code session to a remote server, conversation included
item.description: Move a running Claude Code or Codex session from your Mac to a Linux box over SSH, with the branch, uncommitted files and conversation. DIY and Zoes.

item.title: Vibe Kanban alternative: a local Board for coding agents
item.description: Vibe Kanban is now community maintained and still runs locally. If you want a free, MIT desktop app whose Board starts each ticket in its own git worktree, compare Zoes.

item.title: How to clean up the git worktrees your coding agents leave behind
item.description: Find, measure and remove the worktrees Claude Code, Codex and Cursor leave on disk, what each tool cleans up on its own, and how Zoes deletes them.

item.title: How to run multiple Claude Code agents in parallel
item.description: Run several Claude Code agents on one repo without collisions: one git worktree per agent, by hand or in Zoes, with status, diffs and sessions that keep running.

item.title: Open-source Conductor alternative: Zoes vs Conductor
item.description: Zoes vs Conductor for parallel coding agents: license, price, platforms, supported agents, and what happens to local sessions when you close the app.

item.title: T3 Code alternative: Zoes vs T3 Code
item.description: Zoes vs T3 Code, two free MIT apps for coding agents: platforms, agents, phone apps, what happens when you close the window, and when T3 Code fits better.

item.title: Crystal is now Nimbalyst: options for parallel Claude Code and Codex sessions
item.description: Crystal was deprecated in February 2026 and replaced by Nimbalyst. Your options, including Zoes, a free MIT app for parallel agents in git worktrees.

item.title: Best tools to run multiple coding agents in parallel on Mac (2026), compared fairly
item.description: Eight desktop apps for running coding agents in parallel, compared from their own sites: Zoes, Conductor, Paradev, Synara, Orca, Zeron, MonoCode and T3 Code.

item.title: Keep coding agents running after you close the window
item.description: Why agents stop when a window closes, and how Zoes's daemon, pocketd, keeps Claude Code, Codex and other sessions and automations running.

item.title: A free, open-source agent workspace with no paid tier
item.description: What free means across open-source agent workspaces like Paradev, Synara and T3 Code, and what Zoes includes at $0: automations, Board, SSH hosts and the CLI.

item.title: Native, not Electron: a Rust/GPUI app for your coding agents
item.description: Why Zoes's desktop app is Rust on GPUI with a Go daemon and no Electron or Tauri, and how other native-minded agent apps compare.

item.title: Run multiple Codex CLI agents in git worktrees
item.description: Run several Codex CLI agents on one repository without collisions: one git worktree per agent, by hand or in Zoes, side by side with Claude Code.

item.title: Script coding agents from your shell with zoes session wait
item.description: Start Claude Code or Codex in a new git worktree from a script, send a prompt, and branch on the exit code of zoes session wait. Copy-paste recipes.
